definitions.explanation: A formal or polite way to say one has forgotten something. Commonly used in business or formal settings as a humble expression when admitting to having forgotten.

examples.japanese: {失念|しつねん}しておりました。
{名前|なまえ}を{失念|しつねん}してしまいました。
examples.english: I'm sorry, I've forgotten the name.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}の{日程|にってい}を{失念|しつねん}しており、{大変|たいへん}{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございません。
examples.english: I deeply apologize for having forgotten the date of the important meeting.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
{失念|しつねん} is a formal and somewhat humble way to say "I forgot." It is most commonly used in business correspondence, emails, and formal spoken language. Using {失念|しつねん} instead of {忘|わす}れる shows self-awareness and politeness when admitting a mistake.

REGISTER:
This is a formal word. In casual conversation, {忘|わす}れる is standard. {失念|しつねん} would sound stiff or overly formal among friends.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {忘|わす}れる: to forget (everyday word)
- {度忘|どわす}れ: a momentary lapse of memory, tip-of-the-tongue forgetting
